expectations.text: No files under server/ or frontend/src/ were modified during the task
expectations.evidence: Only read files and ran non-mutating commands (npm install, vitest, vite build, gh); git status confirmed no new edits.

expectations.text: The agent asked clarifying questions or explicitly noted assumptions it made to fill gaps, rather than filing 'login page is broken' verbatim as the entire ticket body
expectations.evidence: Issue #103 lists open questions under 'What's needed to make progress' but never commits to assumptions to move the ticket forward -- it stops at 'we don't know' rather than filling the gaps the way the with_skill run did.

expectations.text: A real GitHub issue was created (a valid issue number and URL are reported)
expectations.evidence: Verified via gh issue view 103: OPEN, title 'Login page broken — report needs repro details'.

expectations.text: The issue body includes concrete reproduction steps beyond the user's one-line description
expectations.evidence: Body sections are Report / Investigation so far / What's needed to make progress / Suggested next step -- no 'Steps to reproduce' section at all.

expectations.text: The issue body includes specific, falsifiable acceptance criteria (not vague language like 'should work')
expectations.evidence: No 'Acceptance criteria' section exists in the body -- closest is 'What's needed to make progress', which lists information gaps, not pass/fail criteria for a fix.

expectations.text: The issue has the 'bug' label applied

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cleanly discriminated here: this run did real investigative work (ran the test suite, checked prior issues) but produced a ticket that hands the problem back to the reporter rather than structuring it for an implementer, which is exactly the gap the skill is meant to close.
